column1: MOT evaluation history and benchmark methodology
column4: Defines populations, the ten-column submission format, the annotation protocol and the visibility field. Fixes the format in which a submitted row is expressed, and that format has no field for row origin.
Defines what is computed from a submitted file and how metrics are combined. Each scores every row of the file; none reads where a row came from.

Reports the stages themselves and ablates their effect on the reporting system's own score. Establishes score change; does not characterise the added rows, nor the effect on a comparison between systems.
Supplies the implementations whose transitions are audited here. Documents method design; post-processing is described where it is described at all, not recorded per submission.

Holds systems fixed and varies the protocol, the data or the ranking rule; one line makes the suitability of the validation data itself the measurement. Varies what is done to a prediction file during scoring, or the data scored against, not what produced the file.

Defines leakage and shows that correcting it moves rankings; also establishes that selecting against held-out scores biases what is then reported on them, and that adaptive reuse of a holdout erodes its validity without any training-data leak. Concerns the information a method consumed, which is the eligibility axis here, not the composition of its output.

column1: Prediction, data and model provenance and lineage
column4: Domain-general models represent produced artifacts, the activities generating them and the derivations relating them, and experiment-metadata systems do record a prediction as an artifact, with the model and dataset that produced it; later taxonomies and end-to-end pipeline provenance extend that bookkeeping across the lifecycle. What none of them records is the post-inference transformation applied to a submitted prediction file, or the link from a reported benchmark score to the exact state that was scored.
Specifies what a dataset, model, challenge or evaluation report should disclose. Specifies disclosure, not a measurement, and none names the artifact the reported number was computed on.
Defines the estimand as the quantity an analysis is meant to estimate. Supplies the vocabulary for the eligibility criterion; says nothing about prediction files.
Supplies the resampling unit and the treatment of dependent multi-system comparison. Methodological input to how the margins here are reported; not about provenance.

column1: Sensitivity to labels, aggregation, missingness, operational definitions
column4: Shows that annotation ambiguity, aggregation rules, data composition and the choice of corpus itself move conclusions. Motivates the gate sweep and the scoreable-reference definition; the object is the reference or the aggregation, not the submitted file.

column1: Recent adjacent work in vision and machine-learning venues
column4: Shows that reported rankings depend on the evaluation setup and that detector quality confounds tracker comparison. Motivates holding the detector fixed; neither examines the transition producing the evaluated file.
